description: MY FILED REMEDY WAS WRONG AND WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A NO-OP. I hypothesised the popup was opened after an await, losing the user-gesture context, and prescribed opening it synchronously and setting location once the link resolves. SpeakerRecord.tsx:161-183 ALREADY DOES EXACTLY THAT. The real defect: window.open('about:blank','_blank','noopener,noreferrer') returns NULL under noopener — the tab is created but no handle comes back — so the synchronous path cannot run and control falls to an after-await window.open that the popup blocker suppresses. Measured by the sweep in a local file:// page: noopener -> null, plain -> handle, setLocation -> ok.
correct_fix: drop noopener,noreferrer from the FIRST open so a navigable handle returns, then sever with previewWindow.opener = null; the preview URL is same-origin so noopener was defensive rather than load-bearing. Remove the after-await fallback entirely — it cannot work by construction and is what made the failure silent.
lesson: A remedy filed from a plausible mechanism, built without verification, produces a passing test against unchanged behaviour. Requiring the cause to be measured before the patch is what caught this.

'Elements never jump' produced a WORSE failure than the jump it prevented. A fixed-height error note reserved one line; nothing bounded what a rejection echoed back (no maxlength, noValidate form, whole value quoted by both client and API), so a 254-character paste overran it and overflow:hidden ate the rest with no sign — silently eaten text, in exactly the case the note exists for.
resolution: Fixed at the source rather than the screen: describeRejectedEmail() caps the quote at 48 chars and is used by the API path too, so the error FIELD is bounded rather than only its container; maxLength on the input; the note reserves three lines and scrolls rather than hiding.
candidate_rule: Reserving space must never mean hiding overflow. A reserved slot needs a bounded value to put in it — bound the content at its source, and let the slot scroll rather than clip. Otherwise the anti-jump rule buys stillness with silence.
proposed_home: DESIGN.md craft rules, or the CLAUDE.md 'UI: Elements Never Jump' section which currently says only 'reserve space for swapped text (min-heights)'

diagnosed_by: Defect Sweep 2 (surface:339), source read, not built
finding:
NOT the card — the gallery, with two independent causes, neither fixable by sizing. (1) STRUCTURAL: src/lib/public-site.ts ~1075-1088 builds speakersById from every published session and returns the whole collection — no LIMIT, slice, page or cap anywhere in the path. Height is therefore a function of how many speakers a conference published, so any fixed number is right for exactly one conference on one day; EMBED_SNIPPET_HEIGHT_PX.speakers cannot be tuned into correctness. (2) DEFAULT: defaultEmbedFields() (public-site.ts:175) returns every field for the kind, which for speakers includes bio, rendered raw as

{speaker.bio}

with no max-height or line-clamp.
decisive_asymmetry: The SESSIONS embed already solved this: long session text goes through publicAbstractSnippet (public-site.ts:678) with ABSTRACT_SNIPPET_CHARS and a head/rest clip. Speaker bio has no equivalent. Same product, one surface clamps its long prose and the other does not — which is why agenda fits 720px and speakers cannot fit 900.
measurement_caution: The 2276px@600 / 2432px@375 figures I relayed should NOT be used to choose a height. .embed-speaker-grid is repeat(auto-fit, minmax(190px,1fr)), so 375px resolves to one column where 600px gives two, and the narrower capture should be roughly double rather than 7% taller. Either the column count is not changing where the CSS says it should, or the two were captured differently. The diagnosis is unaffected — unbounded is unbounded.
options: 1) cap at N and link out to the full /speakers directory — fits a stated height honestly and is the only option that makes the CURRENT fixed-height snippet truthful; 2) fixed height with an internal scroll region — keeps everyone, costs a nested scrollbar inside an iframe on a stranger's page; 3) postMessage auto-resize — explicitly rejected by the EMB-15 fix already merged, requires host cooperation a paste-this-snippet product cannot assume.
recommendation: Option 1, plus clamp the bio the way abstracts already are and make bio off-by-default for the speakers kind. The clamp is a strict improvement independent of which option is chosen, and it closes the unbounded-per-card half.
